C.f: Antonio Valdes and Consuelo Gomez married in 1971 and had five children. The marriage was declared void under Article 36 (psychological incapacity). The trial court ordered the liquidation of their properties under Article 147 and the rules on co-ownership. Valdes argued that Articles 50–52, 102, and 129 of the Family Code should govern instead.
C.r: Article 147 governs. Property acquired during the union is presumed acquired through joint efforts and owned in equal shares, and is liquidated under the rules on co-ownership. Articles 50–52, 102, and 129 apply to voidable marriages and to the void subsequent marriage under Article 40, not to an Article 36 marriage.
C.d: Void marriage between parties capacitated to marry each other → Art. 147 co-ownership, liquidated by co-ownership rules.
C.iss: What rules govern the property relations of spouses whose marriage is void under Article 36?

C.f: Alain and Ma. Caridad Diño's marriage was declared void under Article 36. The trial court ruled that the decree of nullity would issue only after the liquidation, partition, and distribution of their properties under Article 147.
C.r: No. The requirement that liquidation and partition come before the decree (Articles 50 and 51) applies only to marriages declared void under Article 40 and to voidable marriages under Article 45. For a marriage void under Article 36, the property is governed by Article 147 and the decree may issue without prior partition.
C.d: The “partition before decree” rule applies only to Art. 40 and Art. 45 cases, not Art. 147 cases.
C.iss: Must partition be completed before the decree of nullity issues in an Article 147 case?

C.f: Lupo Atienza, a married man, lived with Yolanda De Castro. A property was bought during their relationship and registered in Yolanda's name. Lupo claimed co-ownership, saying he provided the money. Yolanda showed that the funds came from her own resources.
C.r: No. Because Lupo was married to someone else, Article 148 applies. Only property acquired through actual joint contribution is co-owned, and Lupo failed to prove that he contributed. The property belongs to Yolanda.
C.d: Under Art. 148, co-ownership needs PROOF of actual contribution; there is no presumption of joint efforts.
C.iss: Is Lupo a co-owner of the property?

C.f: Two women lived together as a couple and acquired a house and lot in Quezon City, registered in one partner's name. When the relationship ended, the other partner claimed she contributed to acquiring and improving the property. The registered owner had signed a written acknowledgment of that contribution.
C.r: Yes. Same-sex partners who live together may acquire co-ownership rights under Article 148, provided actual contribution is proved. The signed acknowledgment was strong evidence of contribution, so co-ownership was recognized. The ruling concerns property rights only; it does not recognize same-sex marriage.
C.d: Art. 148 covers same-sex cohabitation, subject to proof of actual contribution.
C.iss: May Article 148 apply to same-sex partners, and was actual contribution proved?

C.n: Homeowners Savings & Loan Bank v. Dailo
C.f: During his marriage to Miguela, Marcelino Dailo, without her knowledge, authorized another person to mortgage their conjugal house and lot to secure a loan from the bank. The loan was unpaid, the bank foreclosed, and Marcelino died. Miguela sued to annul the mortgage.
C.r: (1) No. Under Article 124, a disposition or encumbrance of conjugal property without the other spouse's consent is void in its entirety. The husband has no specific share to mortgage before liquidation, because the conjugal partnership is not a co-ownership. (2) No. The bank did not prove that the loan redounded to the benefit of the family.
C.d: Encumbrance of conjugal property without the other spouse's consent is VOID as a whole, not just as to the other's half.
C.iss: (1) Is the mortgage valid at least as to the husband's share? (2) Is the conjugal partnership liable for the loan?

C.f: Alfredo Ching, a married man, signed as surety for loans of a corporation where he was an officer. When the corporation defaulted, the creditor levied on the conjugal properties of Alfredo and his wife.
C.r: No. When a spouse acts as surety or guarantor for another's debt, benefit to the family is not presumed and must be proved. Incidental benefits, like keeping his job or a rise in the value of his shares, are not enough. It is different when a spouse borrows for his own business or profession, where benefit is presumed.
C.d: Surety for a third party's loan → no presumption of family benefit. Loan for one's own business → benefit presumed.
C.iss: Is the conjugal partnership liable for the husband's obligation as surety for a corporation?

C.f: Eduardo Dewara was convicted of serious physical injuries through reckless imprudence for running over Ronnie Lamela, and was ordered to pay damages. He had no exclusive property. The sheriff levied on a lot registered in his wife's name, which she claimed was her paraphernal property.
C.r: The lot was presumed conjugal because it was acquired during the marriage and its exclusive character was not proved. Under Article 122, the husband's civil liability from a crime may be charged against the conjugal partnership when he has no exclusive property, but only after the Article 121 charges are covered, and the payment is treated as an advance deducted from his share at liquidation.
C.d: Personal liabilities from a crime may be advanced by the CPG if the spouse has no exclusive property, after Art. 121 charges, deducted at liquidation.
C.iss: May the lot be levied on to satisfy the husband's civil liability from his crime?

C.f: A judgment for damages from a 1976 vehicular accident was rendered against Jose Modequillo. To enforce it, the sheriff levied on his residential house and lot in 1988. He claimed the property was a family home exempt from execution under the Family Code, which took effect on August 3, 1988.
C.r: No. The residence became a family home by operation of law when the Family Code took effect. But the exemption does not cover debts incurred before that date. Article 162 does not make the exemption retroactive to earlier liabilities. Since the liability arose in 1976, the property is not exempt.
C.d: Existing residences became family homes on August 3, 1988, but the exemption does not apply to debts incurred before then.
C.iss: Is the house and lot exempt from execution as a family home?

C.f: Marcelino Dario died in 1987, leaving his wife Perla and two sons. Years later, Perla and one son sought partition of the family home. The other son objected, saying his minor son, who lived in the house, was a beneficiary, so the home could not be partitioned.
C.r: No. A beneficiary must (1) be related as listed in Article 154, (2) live in the family home, and (3) depend on the head of the family for legal support. The grandson depends for support on his own father, not on the head of the family. Since more than 10 years had passed since the death and there was no qualified minor beneficiary, the family home could be partitioned.
C.d: A minor in the house is not a “minor beneficiary” unless he depends on the head of the family for legal support.
C.iss: Does the presence of the minor grandson prevent the partition of the family home?

C.f: Araceli De Mesa issued a bouncing check to Claudio Acero. Acero obtained judgment, and the spouses' house and lot was levied on and sold at auction to Acero. Years later, the spouses sought to annul the sale, claiming the property was their family home and exempt.
C.r: No. The exemption is not automatic in effect; it must be claimed and proved at the time of the levy or within a reasonable time before the sale. The spouses failed to raise it then and are barred by laches.
C.d: The family-home exemption must be raised at the levy or before the sale; otherwise it is waived.
C.iss: May the spouses still invoke the family-home exemption?

C.f: Vitug borrowed money from Abuda and secured the loan with a mortgage on his property, which he later claimed was his family home. He failed to pay, and Abuda foreclosed.
C.r: No. Under Article 155(3), the family home is not exempt from debts secured by mortgages on the premises, whether before or after its constitution. The owner voluntarily mortgaged it.
C.d: A family home voluntarily mortgaged can be foreclosed (Art. 155(3)).
C.iss: Can the family-home exemption defeat the foreclosure?

C.f: Spouses Hontiveros sued Augusto's brother and the brother's wife for damages. The trial court dismissed the case for failure to allege earnest efforts toward a compromise as required by Article 151 in a verified complaint.
C.r: No. Article 151 applies only to suits exclusively among members of the same family as listed in Article 150. The brother's wife is a sister-in-law, who is not a family member under Article 150, so the requirement does not apply. A defect in verification is also a formal one that may be corrected.
C.d: Including a non-family member (e.g., an in-law) takes the suit outside Art. 151.
C.iss: Was dismissal under Article 151 proper?

C.f: Pedro Gayon sued his deceased brother's widow and heirs over property. The trial court dismissed the case because the complaint did not allege earnest efforts toward a compromise between family members.
C.r: No. The enumeration of family relations is exclusive. Sisters-in-law and brothers-in-law are not included, so the requirement does not apply.
C.d: In-laws are not family members for Art. 150–151 purposes; the list is strictly construed.
C.iss: Is a sister-in-law a member of the family for purposes of the earnest-efforts requirement?

C.f: William Liyao Jr. was born to Corazon Garcia while she was still married to Ramon Yulo, although she lived with William Liyao. After William Liyao died, the child, through his mother, sued for recognition as Liyao's illegitimate son.
C.r: No. A child born during a valid marriage is presumed the legitimate child of the husband, Ramon Yulo. Only the husband, or his heirs in the cases allowed by law, may impugn that legitimacy. The child cannot choose his own filiation or attack his legitimacy collaterally.
C.d: Only the husband (or his heirs in limited cases) may impugn legitimacy; the child cannot claim another father while the presumption stands.
C.iss: May the child establish illegitimate filiation with William Liyao?

C.n: De Jesus v. Estate of Dizon
C.f: Jacqueline and Jinkie De Jesus were born during the marriage of Danilo and Carolina De Jesus. They later claimed to be the illegitimate children of Juan Dizon, who had signed a notarized acknowledgment, and sued for partition of his estate.
C.r: No. They are presumed legitimate children of Danilo. Their legitimacy must first be impugned in a direct action by the proper party; it cannot be attacked collaterally in a partition case.
C.d: Legitimacy cannot be attacked collaterally.
C.iss: May the children claim to be Dizon's illegitimate children in an action for partition?

C.f: Gerardo Concepcion married Ma. Theresa Almonte, and they had a son. Gerardo later learned that Theresa was still married to Mario Gopiao, so their marriage was void for bigamy. He then claimed rights over the child as his son.
C.r: The boy is the legitimate child of Theresa and her lawful husband, Mario Gopiao, because he was born during their valid, subsisting marriage. The presumption could only be impugned by Mario, who never did. Gerardo, a stranger to the child under the law, had no right to visitation as a father.
C.d: The presumption of legitimacy favors the valid marriage; a child cannot be made illegitimate by the mother's or another man's claims.
C.iss: Whose legitimate child is the boy?

C.f: Rosendo Alba, a minor, sued Rosendo Herrera for recognition and support. Herrera denied paternity. The trial court ordered DNA paternity testing. Herrera argued it violated his right against self-incrimination and his privacy.
C.r: Yes. DNA testing is a valid and admissible means of proving paternity, falling under “other means allowed by the Rules of Court and special laws.” Ordering it does not violate the right against self-incrimination or privacy.
C.d: DNA evidence is admissible to prove or disprove filiation.
C.iss: Is DNA testing a valid and admissible means to prove filiation?

C.f: Joanna Diaz, a minor, sued Rogelio Ong for compulsory recognition and support. Rogelio died while the case was pending. The Court of Appeals ordered DNA analysis. His estate argued that DNA testing was impossible after death.
C.r: Yes. DNA may be obtained from biological samples of the deceased or from his relatives. Death does not bar DNA testing.
C.d: The alleged father's death does not prevent DNA testing.
C.iss: Can DNA testing be ordered after the alleged father's death?

C.f: Monina Jison sued Francisco Jison for recognition as his illegitimate daughter. She showed that he paid for her schooling, employed her, and that his relatives and employees treated her as his daughter over many years.
C.r: Yes. Through his acts and those of his family, she proved open and continuous possession of the status of an illegitimate child, by preponderance of evidence.
C.d: Open and continuous possession of status is proved by the parent's consistent, continuous treatment of the child as his own.
C.iss: Did Monina prove her illegitimate filiation?

C.f: Mirasol Baring and her son Randy sued Antonio Perla for support, claiming he was Randy's father. Their main evidence was Randy's birth certificate and baptismal certificate naming Antonio as father. Antonio did not sign or participate in either document.
C.r: No. A birth certificate that the alleged father did not sign or help prepare is not competent evidence of paternity. A baptismal certificate is also insufficient. Without proof of filiation, there is no basis for support.
C.d: A birth certificate without the father's signature or participation does not prove paternity.
C.iss: Was Randy's filiation with Antonio proved?

C.f: Rodolfo Aguilar claimed to be the son of spouses Alfredo Aguilar and Candelaria Siasat. His birth records had been destroyed. He presented Alfredo's SSS Form E-1, signed by Alfredo, naming Rodolfo as his son.
C.r: Yes. The SSS form signed by Alfredo is an admission of filiation in a public document or a private handwritten instrument signed by the parent, which is primary evidence under Article 172. No separate action is needed.
C.d: A form signed by the parent acknowledging the child is primary evidence of filiation.
C.iss: Is the signed SSS form enough to prove legitimate filiation?

C.f: Jenie Dela Cruz was pregnant by Christian Aquino, who died before the child was born. Christian had written an unsigned handwritten autobiography acknowledging the coming child. The civil registrar refused to register the child under Christian's surname.
C.r: Yes, under the special circumstances. Where the father died before the child's birth, an unsigned handwritten instrument may be accepted if corroborated by other evidence. The general rule remains that a private handwritten instrument used as the sole basis must be signed.
C.d: Unsigned handwritten acknowledgment may suffice if corroborated, especially when the father died before the birth.
C.iss: May an unsigned handwritten instrument support the child's use of the father's surname?

C.f: Grace Grande and Patricio Antonio had two children outside marriage. Antonio, who recognized them, sued to have the children use his surname and to get custody.
C.r: No. Under Article 176 as amended by RA 9255, illegitimate children “may” use the father's surname if he recognized them. The word is permissive; the choice belongs to the child, not the father. The children remain under the mother's parental authority.
C.d: Using the father's surname is the illegitimate child's option, not the father's right.
C.iss: Can the father compel his illegitimate children to use his surname?

C.f: Bernie Santiago claimed to be the biological father of a child whose birth certificate named the mother's husband as the father. He sought to establish his filiation with the child and to correct the birth certificate.
C.r: Yes. The Court allowed the proceedings to continue and remanded the case for further proceedings, including DNA analysis. It did not declare Bernie the father; it allowed evidence to be received and weighed.
C.d: Scientific evidence may be received on biological parentage; a less rigid approach than an absolute bar.
C.iss: May the proceedings continue, including DNA analysis?

C.f: James Cua Ko sought court approval of his voluntary recognition of a child born while the mother was still married to another man.
C.r: No. His petition was denied because it was an unauthorized collateral attack on the child's legitimacy. But the Court stressed that legitimacy and filiation are distinct and recognized the child's own right to establish her biological filiation if she chooses.
C.d: The alleged father cannot attack legitimacy collaterally; the child keeps her own right to establish biological filiation.
C.iss: May an alleged biological father recognize a child born during the mother's subsisting marriage?

C.n: In re Adoption of Stephanie Garcia
C.f: Honorato Catindig adopted his illegitimate daughter Stephanie and asked that she use her mother's surname, Garcia, as her middle name.
C.r: Yes. No law prohibits it, and allowing it serves the child's welfare and keeps her ties to her mother's family, which matter for succession.
C.d: An adopted child may use the biological mother's surname as middle name.
C.iss: May an adopted child use her biological mother's surname as her middle name?

C.f: Isabelita Lahom adopted Jose Melvin Sibulo in 1972. After the 1998 adoption law took effect, she sought to rescind the adoption because of his ingratitude.
C.r: No. The adopter's right to rescind under the old law was not a vested right, and the new law grants the right to rescind only to the adoptee. The adopter's remedy is to disinherit the adoptee for causes recognized by law. The current law, RA 11642, keeps this rule.
C.d: Only the adoptee may rescind; the adopter's remedy is disinheritance.
C.iss: May the adopter rescind the adoption?

C.f: Jose Castro, a married man, adopted his illegitimate son without the knowledge or consent of his wife and their legitimate daughter. They later sought to annul the adoption.
C.r: No. The consent of the adopter's spouse and of his legitimate children aged 10 or older is required. Their lack of notice and consent meant the court did not acquire jurisdiction, and the adoption was obtained through extrinsic fraud.
C.d: Adoption without the required consent of the spouse and legitimate children is void.
C.iss: Is the adoption valid?

C.f: Ten-year-old Adelberto Bundoc shot and killed Jennifer Tamargo with an air rifle. Before the shooting, spouses Rapisura had filed a petition to adopt him; the adoption was granted after the shooting. The victim's parents sued.
C.r: The biological parents. Parental authority and actual custody were with them when the tort happened. The retroactive effect of the adoption decree cannot impose liability on adopters who had no actual custody at that time.
C.d: Vicarious liability follows actual parental authority and custody at the time of the act.
C.iss: Who is liable for the child's tort: the biological parents or the adopters?

C.f: Cheryl Lim and her children sued her husband Edward and his parents for support. Edward's income was not enough to support the children.
C.r: The grandparents are liable to support the grandchildren, because the obligation passes to ascendants in the nearest degree when the parents cannot provide. They are not liable to support Cheryl, their daughter-in-law, who is not among those entitled under Article 195.
C.d: Grandparents may be ordered to support grandchildren when the parents cannot; in-laws are not owed support.
C.iss: Are the paternal grandparents liable to support the grandchildren and their mother?

C.f: Twin daughters sought support for their college education from their father, Federico Delgado, and their wealthy paternal grandfather, Francisco Delgado. Federico had little means.
C.r: Yes. Support includes education even beyond the age of majority. Since the father could not provide it, the obligation fell on the grandfather as the ascendant in the next degree. His option to support them in his home was unavailable because of the obstacles in the relationship.
C.d: Support includes higher education; grandparents answer when parents cannot.
C.iss: Is the grandfather liable for support, including college education?

C.f: A mother sued Manuel De Asis for support of her minor child. She later withdrew the case, agreeing not to pursue it because he denied paternity. When she refiled, he invoked res judicata.
C.r: No. The right to future support cannot be renounced or compromised. The mother's agreement to drop the earlier case was void and cannot bar the child's action.
C.d: Future support cannot be waived or compromised.
C.iss: Does the earlier withdrawal bar the new action for support?

C.f: Franklin Hirsch and Agnes Gamboa-Hirsch separated. The Court of Appeals awarded joint custody of their daughter, who was below 7 years old.
C.r: No. Under Article 213, no child under 7 shall be separated from the mother unless the court finds compelling reasons, such as neglect, abandonment, unemployment, immorality, drug addiction, or insanity. None was shown, so custody belongs to the mother.
C.d: Tender-age rule: a child under 7 stays with the mother absent compelling reasons.
C.iss: Was joint custody of a child under 7 proper?

C.f: Leouel Santos sought custody of his son, who was being raised by the boy's maternal grandparents while the mother was abroad.
C.r: The father. Parents have the natural and primary right to custody. Grandparents exercise substitute parental authority only when the parents are dead, absent, or unsuitable, which was not shown.
C.d: Parents prevail over grandparents; substitute authority applies only when parents are dead, absent, or unsuitable.
C.iss: Who has the better right to custody: the father or the grandparents?

C.f: Joey Briones sought custody of his illegitimate son from the boy's mother, Loreta Miguel.
C.r: The mother. Under Article 176, an illegitimate child is under the sole parental authority of the mother. The father's recognition does not give him parental authority, though he may seek visitation rights.
C.d: Illegitimate child → mother's sole parental authority; the father may get only visitation.
C.iss: Who has custody and parental authority over the illegitimate child?

C.f: During a school enrollment campaign, student Sherwin Carpitanos rode a jeep driven by a 15-year-old student. The jeep overturned and Sherwin died. It was later shown that the steering wheel guide had detached.
C.r: No. The school's liability requires that its negligence or the minor's act be the proximate cause of the injury. The proximate cause was the detached steering wheel guide, a mechanical defect, not the school's negligence or the minor's driving.
C.d: Special parental authority liability requires that the negligence or act be the PROXIMATE cause.
C.iss: Is the school liable under its special parental authority?

C.f: Alfredo Amadora was shot by a classmate inside the school auditorium. He had gone to school, after classes had formally ended, to submit a physics report.
C.r: Article 2180 applies to all schools, academic or not. In an academic school, the teacher-in-charge, not the head, is liable; in schools of arts and trades, the head is liable. The student remains in custody while in school for a legitimate purpose, even after classes. Here, however, no negligence of the teacher-in-charge was proved, so no one was held liable.
C.d: Academic school → teacher-in-charge liable; arts and trades → head liable; custody covers legitimate presence in school.
C.iss: Is the school or its teachers liable under Article 2180?

C.f: Wendell Libi, a minor, shot his girlfriend and then himself with his father's gun, which was kept in a place he could reach. The girl's parents sued Wendell's parents.
C.r: Yes. Parents' liability for their minor children's acts is primary, not subsidiary, and they can escape it only by proving the diligence of a good father of a family. Leaving the gun accessible showed lack of diligence.
C.d: Parents' liability for minor children is PRIMARY; the defense is proper diligence.
C.iss: Are the parents liable, and is their liability primary or subsidiary?

C.f: Atty. Adriano Adriano, legally married to Rosario, lived with his common-law partner Fe Valino. When he died, Valino buried him in her family's mausoleum. His wife and children sued to have the remains exhumed and transferred.
C.r: The legal wife. The right and duty follow the order in Article 199: spouse, descendants, ascendants, siblings. A common-law partner has no superior right. There was no clear proof that the deceased wished to be buried with Valino, so the legal family's right prevailed.
C.d: The legal spouse has the first right to make funeral arrangements; a common-law partner does not.
C.iss: Who has the right to make the funeral arrangements?

C.f: Rommel Silverio underwent sex reassignment surgery and petitioned to change his first name and his sex in his birth certificate to female.
C.r: No. No law allows the change of the entry of sex because of sex reassignment; sex is determined at birth. A change of first name also cannot be granted on that basis.
C.d: Sex reassignment is not a ground to change name or sex in the civil register.
C.iss: May the birth certificate be changed because of sex reassignment?

C.f: Jennifer Cagandahan was registered as female but had congenital adrenal hyperplasia, an intersex condition, and developed male characteristics. She petitioned to change her name to Jeff and her sex to male.
C.r: Yes. For a person with an intersex condition, the person's own development and choice may determine the sex to be recorded. The petition was granted through an adversarial proceeding.
C.d: An intersex person may have sex and name entries changed; distinguish from Silverio.
C.iss: May the entries be changed?

C.f: Maria Fe Cantor's husband left after a quarrel. Four years later she sought a declaration of his presumptive death to remarry. Her search consisted of asking relatives and checking some hospitals.
C.r: No. A well-founded belief requires diligent and reasonable efforts to find the absent spouse, judged strictly. Her efforts were passive and insufficient.
C.d: Presumptive death for remarriage needs a well-founded belief shown by diligent, active search.
C.iss: Did she establish a well-founded belief that her husband was dead?

C.f: Merlinda Olaybar discovered that records showed her married to a foreigner she had never met; her signature had been forged. She sought cancellation of the entries in the marriage certificate under Rule 108.
C.r: Rule 108 is proper. The issue was not the validity of a marriage but whether she married at all, given the forged signature. Since an adversarial proceeding was held, the entries could be corrected.
C.d: Rule 108 may correct entries when no marriage actually took place (identity theft), in an adversarial proceeding.
C.iss: Is Rule 108 the proper remedy, or is this a disguised action for nullity of marriage?

C.n: Remo v. Secretary of Foreign Affairs
C.f: Maria Virginia Remo, a married woman whose passport used her husband's surname, asked to revert to her maiden name in her passport while her marriage was still subsisting.
C.r: A married woman may, but is not required to, use her husband's surname. But once she used it in her passport, the passport law allows reverting to her maiden name only in cases of death, divorce, annulment, or nullity. Her request was denied.
C.d: Use of the husband's surname is optional; passport reversion is limited by the passport law.
C.iss: Must a married woman use her husband's surname, and can she revert in her passport?

M.q: Ana and Ben marry without a marriage settlement in 2020. What is their property regime?
M.x: Without a settlement, ACP is the default (Art. 75).

M.q: Their settlement provides for CPG but was signed one day AFTER the wedding. What regime governs?
o: CPG, because they agreed on it
ACP, because the settlement was executed after the marriage
CSP, because the agreement is void
CPG, but only between the spouses
M.x: A settlement must be executed before the marriage (Art. 77). A settlement made after is ineffective, so the default ACP applies.

M.q: A valid written settlement providing for complete separation of property was never registered. A creditor of the husband sues. Which is TRUE?
o: The settlement binds the spouses but not the creditor
The settlement binds everyone because it is in writing
M.x: Registration is needed only to bind third persons (Art. 77). Between the spouses it is valid.

M.q: Which of the following is FALSE about the start of the ACP?
o: It starts at the precise moment the marriage is celebrated
The spouses may agree that it starts one year after the wedding
A stipulation fixing another start date is void
M.x: Art. 88: any stipulation, express or implied, for the commencement of the community at any other time is void.

M.q: Carla's parents donate a car to her and her fiancé in consideration of their wedding, but the wedding is called off. The donation was NOT in a marriage settlement. What is its status?
M.x: Art. 86(1): revocable if the marriage is not celebrated. If the donation had been in the marriage settlement, it would be void under Art. 81.

M.q: Future spouses agree on CPG. In the settlement, the groom donates to the bride 1/3 of his present property. What is the status of the donation?
o: Valid up to 1/5 of his present property; void as to the excess
M.x: Art. 84: when the regime is not ACP, donations between future spouses in the settlement cannot exceed 1/5 of present property; the excess is void.

M.q: Which statement about donations propter nuptias is TRUE?
o: They can never include future property
They may include future property, governed by the rules on wills
Future property may be donated only if the regime is ACP
They need no acceptance at all
M.x: Art. 84, par. 2.

M.q: After the wedding, Dan gives his wife a P2 million condominium as an anniversary gift. Their regime is CSP. Which is TRUE?
o: Valid, because in CSP each spouse owns his property
Valid if they have no children
Void, because donations between spouses during marriage are prohibited
Valid as a moderate gift on family rejoicing
M.x: Art. 87 prohibits donations between spouses during marriage, whatever the regime. A P2 million condo is not a moderate gift.

M.q: Which does NOT belong? (ingratitude of the donee)
o: The donee physically attacks the donor
The donee imputes to the donor a crime the donor committed against the donee's own child
The donee unduly refuses to support the donor
The donee destroys the donor's property
M.x: Imputing a crime is NOT ingratitude when the crime was committed against the donee, his spouse, or children under his authority (Art. 765(2)).

M.q: Elsa (donee) married Fred (donor). Their marriage was annulled because Fred concealed his drug addiction. May Fred revoke his donation propter nuptias to Elsa?
o: Yes, because the marriage was annulled
No, because the donee was in good faith
No, because annulled marriages never affect donations
M.x: Art. 86(3) allows revocation of donations to a donee who acted in bad faith. Elsa was innocent.

M.q: Under ACP, which of the following is EXCLUDED from the community?
o: A house inherited by the wife during the marriage
Jewelry bought by the husband for himself
A lot owned by the husband before the marriage, he having no children
M.x: Gratuitous acquisitions during marriage are excluded (Art. 92(1)). Jewelry is community even if for personal use; pre-marriage property is community unless the spouse has legitimate descendants by a former marriage; winnings are community (Art. 95).

M.q: Under ACP, Gina inherited a rice field during the marriage. The harvest from it is:
o: Gina's exclusive property, unless the testator provided otherwise
M.x: The fruits and income of gratuitously acquired property are also excluded, unless the donor or testator provides that they form part of the community (Art. 92(1)).

M.q: Hector, a widower with two LEGITIMATE children from his first marriage, owns a building and marries Ivy under ACP. The building and its rentals are:
o: Community property, but the rentals are exclusive
M.x: Art. 92(3): property acquired before the marriage by a spouse with legitimate descendants by a former marriage, and its fruits and income, are excluded.

M.q: Same facts, but Hector's two children from his first relationship are ILLEGITIMATE. The building is:
o: Exclusive, but the rentals are community
M.x: Art. 92(3) requires LEGITIMATE descendants. With only illegitimate children, the general rule (Art. 91) applies.

M.q: Under ACP, the husband inherits a lot during the marriage (his exclusive property), sells it, and uses the money to buy a condominium. Following the preferred view, the condominium is:
o: The husband's exclusive property, because it merely replaced his property
Community property, because ACP has no exclusion for property bought with exclusive funds
Owned in proportion to the funds used
M.x: Follow this view: under ACP, property acquired during marriage is community unless the law excludes it; there is no ACP equivalent of Art. 109(4). (The contrary view says it stays exclusive.)

M.q: Which of the following is NOT chargeable to the ACP?
o: Support of the husband's legitimate child from his first marriage
Real property taxes on the wife's exclusive house used by the family
Litigation expenses between the spouses, the suit not being groundless
M.x: Gambling losses are borne by the loser alone (Art. 95).

M.q: Under ACP, the wife, without the husband's consent, borrows P100,000 for a family vacation that the whole family enjoyed. Which is TRUE?
o: The ACP is liable to the extent the family benefited
The husband is liable only if he ratifies it
M.x: Art. 94(3): debts contracted by one spouse without consent are chargeable to the extent the family benefited.

M.q: Under ACP, the husband sells community land without the wife's written consent. The wife learns of it and, a month later and before the buyer withdraws, signs a written acceptance. The sale is:
o: Void and can never be cured
Binding, because the transaction was a continuing offer that she accepted
M.x: Art. 96: a disposition without consent is void, but it is a continuing offer that becomes a binding contract upon the other spouse's acceptance before withdrawal.

M.q: The spouses disagree on how to run the family store, an act of administration. Whose decision prevails, and what is the wife's remedy?
o: The wife's; the husband may sue within 10 years
The husband's; the wife may go to court within 5 years from the contract implementing the decision
Neither; the court decides at once
The husband's; the wife has no remedy
M.x: Art. 96.

M.q: Which does NOT dissolve the ACP?
o: Separation in fact for five years
M.x: Separation in fact does not dissolve the regime (Art. 100).

M.q: In liquidating the ACP, what is the FIRST step?
o: Inventory of the community property and of the exclusive property of each spouse, listed separately

M.q: The couple has three children aged 12, 9, and 5. The two older children choose to stay with the father. The conjugal dwelling goes to:
o: The mother, because one child is below 7
The father, because the majority chose him
The court decides at its discretion
It is sold and the proceeds divided
M.x: Art. 102(6): to the spouse with whom the majority of the common children choose to remain. The 5-year-old is deemed to choose the mother, but the majority (2 of 3) chose the father.

M.q: Liza's husband dies in 2023. There is no judicial settlement and she never liquidates the community. In 2025 she remarries. What is the regime of her new marriage?
o: Whatever they agree on in a settlement
M.x: Art. 103: if the survivor remarries without liquidating within one year, the new marriage is mandatorily governed by complete separation of property.

M.q: Same facts. In 2024, Liza sold a community lot without liquidating. The sale is:
M.x: Art. 103: any disposition or encumbrance of community property without liquidation within one year after death is void.

M.q: Under CPG, the wife sells her pre-marriage lot and buys a car with the money. The car is:
M.x: Art. 109(4): property purchased with exclusive money of a spouse is exclusive. Contrast with ACP.

M.q: Under CPG, which is conjugal property?
o: A house inherited by the husband during the marriage
A lot the husband owned before the marriage
A watch donated to the wife by her sister
M.x: Earnings from labor or profession are conjugal (Art. 117(2)).

M.q: Under CPG, the husband's pre-marriage apartment earns rent during the marriage. The rent is:
M.x: Art. 117(3): net fruits of exclusive property received during marriage are conjugal.

M.q: Before the marriage, Mark bought a lot on installment; full ownership vested in him before the wedding, and the last installments were paid during the marriage with conjugal funds. The lot is:
o: Mark's exclusive property, with reimbursement to the CPG
M.x: Art. 118: if full ownership vested before the marriage, it belongs to the buyer, subject to reimbursement.

M.q: Under CPG, a house worth P3 million (cost plus increase in value) is built with conjugal funds on the wife's lot worth P1 million. Which is TRUE?
o: The lot stays exclusive; the CPG is reimbursed
The whole property becomes conjugal, upon reimbursement to the wife of the lot's value
The wife owns the house and lot
M.x: Art. 120: if the improvement plus increase in value is greater, the entire property becomes conjugal, ownership vesting upon reimbursement at liquidation.

M.q: Which charge applies to the CPG but NOT to the ACP?
o: Taxes and preservation expenses on separate property even if not used by the family
Debts contracted with the other spouse's consent
M.x: Art. 121(5) has no “used by the family” qualifier; Art. 94(5) does.

M.q: Which is FALSE about the CPG?
o: Each spouse retains ownership of his or her exclusive property
Only net gains are divided at dissolution
A spouse needs the other's consent to sell his exclusive property
The partnership starts at the celebration of the marriage
M.x: Art. 111: a spouse may alienate his exclusive property without the other's consent.

M.q: In CPG liquidation, which step comes right AFTER the inventory?
o: Reimbursement of each spouse for exclusive funds used
Crediting to the CPG the amounts it advanced for personal debts of either spouse
M.x: Art. 129 order: inventory → credit advances to the CPG → reimburse spouses → pay debts → deliver exclusive properties → pay for lost movables → divide net profits.

M.q: The husband, as surety, signs for a loan of his friend's company. The company defaults. Is the CPG liable?
o: Yes, benefit to the family is presumed
Yes, because he is the administrator
No, unless the creditor proves the family benefited
M.x: Ayala Investment v. CA: for surety obligations, benefit to the family is not presumed.

M.q: The husband is convicted of reckless imprudence and has no exclusive property. Which is TRUE about his civil liability?
o: The CPG can never pay it
The CPG may pay it after covering Art. 121 charges, as an advance deducted at liquidation
The wife pays it from her exclusive property

M.q: Which is NOT a ground for judicial separation of property for sufficient cause?
o: The spouse was sentenced to a penalty carrying civil interdiction
The spouses have been separated in fact for 6 months
The spouse abused the power of administration given in the settlement
The spouse lost parental authority by court decree
M.x: Separation in fact must be at least ONE year, with reconciliation highly improbable (Art. 135(6)).

M.q: In a petition for judicial separation of property, after the court protects the creditors, what is the NEXT step?
o: Liquidation of the ACP or CPG
The court issues the decree of separation of property
M.x: Sequence: petition → protection of creditors → decree → liquidation. Answer the exact step asked.

M.q: Spouses obtained a voluntary judicial separation of property, then agreed to revive their former regime. Later they want another voluntary separation. Which is TRUE?
o: It may be granted any time
It may be granted after 10 years
No voluntary separation may thereafter be granted
M.x: Art. 141, last ground.

M.q: Under complete separation of property, the wife earns P60,000 and the husband P40,000 monthly. Family expenses are P50,000. How much does each bear between themselves?
M.x: Art. 146: in proportion to income (60:40). To creditors, however, they are solidarily liable.

M.q: Jose and Maria, both single and capacitated to marry each other, live together for 10 years. Maria stays home caring for the household; Jose buys a house with his salary. The house is owned:
o: In proportion to contributions, under Art. 148
M.x: Art. 147: property acquired while living together is presumed by joint efforts; care of the household counts as contribution.

M.q: Same facts, but Jose is married to another woman. The house is:
o: Owned equally by Jose and Maria
Owned only by those who actually contributed, in proportion; Jose's share goes to his ACP or CPG with his lawful wife
Owned by Jose's lawful wife alone
M.x: Art. 148: actual contribution only; homemaking does not count; the married party's share goes to his valid marriage's regime.

M.q: Two women live together as partners and buy a condominium registered in one's name; the other proves she paid 40% of the price. Which is TRUE?
o: Art. 147 applies; they own it equally
Art. 148 applies; she is a co-owner in proportion to her proven contribution
No co-ownership, because same-sex unions are not recognized
M.x: Josef v. Ursua: Art. 148 applies to same-sex cohabitation, subject to proof of actual contribution.

M.q: Under Art. 147, may one partner sell his share in a house they co-own while they are still living together?
o: No, not without the other's consent until the cohabitation ends
M.x: Art. 147: neither party can dispose of his share by acts inter vivos without the other's consent until the cohabitation is terminated.

M.q: Which is NOT a family relation under Art. 150?
o: Brothers and sisters of the half-blood
M.x: The list is exclusive: spouses, parents and children, ascendants and descendants, siblings.

M.q: Liza sues her brother over a parcel of land. Her complaint does not allege earnest efforts toward a compromise. The brother moves to dismiss. Which is TRUE?
o: Dismissal is improper; siblings are not covered
The case should be dismissed unless earnest efforts are shown
The case continues because land is involved
M.x: Art. 151 applies to suits between siblings.

M.q: Same facts, but Liza also sues her brother's wife as co-defendant. Which is TRUE?
o: Art. 151 does not apply because a sister-in-law is not a family member
M.x: Hontiveros; Gayon: including a non-family member takes the case outside Art. 151.

M.q: Which suit between family members does NOT require earnest efforts toward a compromise?
o: Partition of inherited land between siblings
Collection of a loan between spouses
Recovery of possession between parent and child
M.x: Validity of marriage cannot be compromised (Art. 2035 CC), so Art. 151 does not apply.

M.q: Which debt can be enforced against a family home?
o: A credit-card debt incurred after the family home was constituted
Unpaid wages of the carpenters who built the house
A personal loan from a friend, unsecured
A judgment for damages for a tort committed after constitution
M.x: Art. 155(4): debts due laborers, mechanics, builders, materialmen for the construction.

M.q: To sell a family home, whose written consent is required?
o: The constitutor, the spouse, and the majority of the beneficiaries of legal age

M.q: A house became the family home in 1985 and the debt was incurred in 1987. Execution is levied in 2026. Is the house exempt?
o: Yes, because it is a family home
No, because the exemption does not apply to debts incurred before the Family Code took effect
No, because the value exceeds the cap
M.x: Modequillo v. Breva.

M.q: The head of the family dies. His wife, 2 adult sons, and a minor grandson (supported by his own father) live in the house. Five years after the death, may the heirs partition the family home?
o: Yes, the grandson is not a minor beneficiary
No, the family home continues for 10 years from death
Yes, if the court finds compelling reasons
Both B and C are correct
M.x: Art. 159: it continues for 10 years or while there is a minor beneficiary, and heirs cannot partition unless the court finds compelling reasons. Five years have not lapsed.

M.q: Which is TRUE about the family home under the Family Code?
o: It must be registered to be constituted
It is constituted from the time it is occupied as the family residence
A person may have two family homes
It may be constituted on land co-owned with strangers without their consent
M.x: Art. 153; and only one family home per person (Art. 161).

M.q: The spouses failed to claim the family-home exemption during the levy and the auction. Years later they sue to annul the sale. Which is TRUE?
o: The sale is void; the exemption is absolute
The claim is barred; the exemption must be set up at the levy or before the sale
The sale is voidable within 4 years
The creditor must refund the price
M.x: De Mesa v. Acero.

M.q: Which is FALSE about Art. 332 of the Revised Penal Code?
o: A son who steals from his father has no criminal liability
A brother-in-law living apart who swindles his sister-in-law is exempt
A stranger who helps the son is not exempt
M.x: Siblings and in-laws are exempt only if living together.

M.q: Baby Ana was born to Carla during her marriage to Dino. Carla publicly declares that Eric is the father. What is Ana's status?
M.x: Art. 167: a child is legitimate even if the mother declares against it.

M.q: Who may impugn Ana's legitimacy?
o: Dino, or his heirs only in the cases under Art. 171
M.x: Only the husband, and his heirs in limited cases.

M.q: Dino lives in Manila; Ana was born and registered in Cebu. He learns of the birth on Jan. 10, 2026. Until when may he file the action to impugn?
M.x: Art. 170: two years if he resides elsewhere in the Philippines, counted from knowledge of the birth or its recording.

M.q: Which is a ground to impugn legitimacy?
o: The husband was working abroad but came home for a week within the first 120 days of the 300 days before the birth
The husband was in prison throughout the first 120 days of the 300 days before the birth, with no conjugal visits
The child does not look like the husband
M.x: Art. 166(1)(b): spouses living separately so that intercourse was not possible during the first 120 days of the 300 days before the birth.

M.q: Artificial insemination of the wife with donor sperm. The husband consented in a written instrument signed by both before the birth. Which is TRUE?
o: The child must be adopted by the husband
M.x: Art. 164, par. 2.

M.q: Which is PRIMARY evidence of illegitimate filiation?
o: Open and continuous possession of the status
A handwritten letter signed by the father acknowledging the child

M.q: An illegitimate child relies only on open and continuous possession of status. Until when may the action be filed?
o: During the lifetime of the alleged parent
Within 5 years from the parent's death
M.x: Art. 175: when based on secondary evidence, only during the lifetime of the alleged parent.

M.q: A birth certificate names Ramon as the father, but Ramon did not sign it or take part in preparing it. Which is TRUE?
o: It is conclusive proof of paternity
It is not competent proof of Ramon's paternity
M.x: Perla v. Baring.

M.q: Paolo, who recognized his illegitimate son in the birth certificate, demands that the boy use his surname. The mother refuses. Which is TRUE?
o: The boy must use Paolo's surname
The boy may use Paolo's surname; the choice is the child's, not Paolo's
Paolo gets parental authority upon recognition
The court decides by majority vote of the parents
M.x: Grande v. Antonio; Art. 176 (RA 9255).

M.q: Rico (17) and Lea (16), both single, have a child. Two years later they validly marry. Is the child legitimated?
o: No, because they were minors when the child was conceived
Only if they adopt the child
M.x: Art. 177 as amended: legitimation is allowed when the only impediment at conception was minority.

M.q: Sam, married to Tina, has a child with Uma. Later Sam's marriage is declared void and he marries Uma. Is the child legitimated?
o: No, because the parents had an impediment (Sam's existing marriage) at conception
M.x: Art. 177: parents must not have been disqualified by any impediment (other than minority) at conception.

M.q: Legitimation takes effect from:
o: The date of the parents' marriage
The date of the court order
The registration in the civil registry

M.q: Under current law, what is the general minimum age of a Filipino adopter?
M.x: RA 11642: at least 25 years old (27 is for inter-country adopters).

M.q: Vic, 30, wants to adopt Wally, 20. Which is TRUE?
o: Allowed if the 16-year gap is met
Not allowed, because the age gap is only 10 years, unless Vic is Wally's biological parent or the spouse of his parent
Never allowed, because Wally is an adult
M.x: The 16-year difference may be waived only if the adopter is the biological parent or the spouse of the adoptee's parent.

M.q: Spouses Xavier and Yna want to adopt. Xavier alone files to adopt Yna's legitimate son from her first marriage. Which is TRUE?
o: Invalid; spouses must always adopt jointly
Valid; this is an exception to joint adoption
Valid only if Yna is legally separated
M.x: Exception: one spouse adopts the legitimate child of the other.

M.q: Whose consent is NOT required for the adoption of 12-year-old Zoe?
o: Zoe's biological parents (if known and not deprived)
M.x: The adopter's children must consent only if 10 years old or older.

M.q: An adopter wants to undo the adoption because the adoptee has become ungrateful. What is the adopter's remedy?
o: Disinheritance for causes provided by law
Petition to the NACC to revoke
M.x: Only the adoptee may rescind (Lahom v. Sibulo; RA 11642).

M.q: Which is NOT an effect of adoption?
o: The adoptee becomes the legitimate child of the adopter
Legal ties with the biological parents are severed, even if the biological parent is the adopter's spouse
The adoptee may use the adopter's surname
M.x: Ties are NOT severed with a biological parent who is the adopter's spouse.

M.q: Ten-year-old Ben shot a playmate. Before the incident, spouses Cruz had petitioned to adopt him; the adoption was granted after. Who is liable?
o: The Cruz spouses, because adoption retroacts
Ben's biological parents, who had parental authority and custody at the time
No one, because Ben is a minor
M.x: Tamargo v. CA.

M.q: Both parents of a child died last month. When can adoption proceedings for the child be started?
o: After 6 months from the parents' death
Only after a guardian is appointed
M.x: RA 11642: no proceedings within 6 months from the death of the parents in that category.

M.q: Which pair is NOT obliged to support each other under Arts. 195–196?
M.x: In-laws are not in the list.

M.q: Kaye, 20, is in college. Her father says support ended when she turned 18. Which is TRUE?
o: Support includes education even beyond majority
Support continues only if she is unemployed
She must sue her mother first

M.q: Since January, Lea has needed support from her father. She sent him a written demand in April and sued in June. From when is support PAYABLE?
M.x: Art. 203: demandable from the time of need, but payable only from the date of judicial or extrajudicial demand.

M.q: Mother and father sign an agreement waiving the child's FUTURE support in exchange for a lump sum. Which is TRUE?
o: Void, because future support cannot be waived or compromised
Valid if approved by the barangay
M.x: De Asis v. CA; Art. 2035 CC.

M.q: Which may be validly compromised?
o: The amount of future support for 5 years
M.x: Support in arrears may be renounced, compromised, or compensated.

M.q: Both parents of a child are unemployed and without means. Who is next liable for the child's support?
o: The grandparents (ascendants in the nearest degree)
M.x: Art. 199 order; Lim v. Lim; Mangonon v. CA.

M.q: A father has limited means. Both his wife and his 5-year-old son need support. Who is preferred?
o: The wife, because she is first in Art. 199
The son, a child under parental authority
M.x: Art. 200: when the concurrent recipients are the spouse and a child under parental authority, the child is preferred.

M.q: Under ACP, the husband must support his legitimate mother. He has no separate property. Which is TRUE?
o: The ACP may advance it, deducted from his share at liquidation

M.q: A creditor of a child attaches the monthly support money the child receives from his father. Which is TRUE?
o: Not allowed; support is exempt from attachment and execution

M.q: Separated parents both want custody of their 5-year-old daughter. The mother works full time. Who gets custody?
o: The father, because he is home more
The mother, unless the court finds compelling reasons
M.x: Art. 213; Gamboa-Hirsch. Working full time is not a compelling reason.

M.q: The parents of 10-year-old Mia died. Her grandmother (65), her brother (23), and her aunt who actually cares for her all want parental authority. Who has the first right?
o: The brother, as oldest sibling over 21
M.x: Art. 216 order: surviving grandparent, oldest sibling over 21, actual custodian over 21.

M.q: During a field trip, a 14-year-old student pushes a classmate off a ledge. Who is principally liable?
o: The school, its administrators, and teachers, solidarily
No one, because it was outside the school
M.x: Art. 218–219: special parental authority covers authorized activities outside the school; the school is principally and solidarily liable, the parents subsidiarily.

M.q: Which is TRUE about an illegitimate child's parental authority?
o: It is exercised jointly if the father recognized the child
The father exercises it if he gives support
The court assigns it at birth
M.x: Art. 176; Briones v. Miguel.

M.q: Which permanently terminates parental authority?
o: Judicial declaration of the parent's absence
M.x: Art. 228: death of the parents, death of the child, or emancipation. The others (Art. 229) may be revived by final judgment.

M.q: A parent is found to have allowed the child to be sexually abused. What happens to parental authority?
o: It is suspended until the child is 18

M.q: A minor's property earns P80,000 a year. The parents act as legal guardians. What must they do?
o: Post a bond of at least 10% of the property's value or annual income
M.x: Art. 225: if the property or income exceeds P50,000, a bond of at least 10% is required.

M.q: A teacher spanks a pupil for misbehavior. Which is TRUE?
o: Allowed, as part of special parental authority
Prohibited; corporal punishment by teachers is not allowed

M.q: Ella turned 18 and wants to marry without telling her parents. Which is TRUE?
o: She needs no consent because she is emancipated
She still needs parental consent until 21
She needs consent only if still studying
M.x: Emancipation is at 18, but parental consent to marry is required until 21.

M.q: The Family Code took effect in 1988. Which is TRUE about its retroactive effect?
o: It never applies to marriages before 1988
It applies retroactively unless it prejudices vested or acquired rights
It applies only to property relations
It applies only if the spouses consent

M.q: A man dies, survived by his legal wife and his common-law partner. They disagree on where to bury him; he left no instructions. Who decides?
o: The common-law partner, who lived with him
M.x: Art. 305 with Art. 199; Valino v. Adriano.

M.q: Two children of the deceased, of the same degree, disagree on the funeral. The spouse is dead. Who is preferred?
M.x: Art. 305: among descendants of the same degree, the oldest is preferred.

M.q: A married woman wants to keep using only her maiden name. Which is TRUE?
o: She must use her husband's surname
She may keep her maiden name; using the husband's surname is optional
M.x: Art. 370 uses “may”; Remo v. Secretary of Foreign Affairs.

M.q: After annulment, the wife was the innocent party. Which is TRUE about her surname?
o: She must resume her maiden name
She may resume her maiden name or keep her former husband's surname, unless the court decrees otherwise or either remarries
She must keep her husband's surname

M.q: Rey left home without news; he left no administrator. How long before he may be judicially declared absent?
M.x: Art. 384: 2 years without news (5 years if he left an administrator).

M.q: Sonia's husband was aboard a vessel lost at sea 4 years ago. For purposes of REMARRIAGE, which is TRUE?
o: She may remarry without any court action
She needs a judicial declaration of presumptive death; 2 years' absence suffices in danger-of-death cases
M.x: Art. 41 FC: 4 years, or 2 years where there is danger of death, plus a summary judicial declaration. (Art. 391 CC's 4 years governs other purposes.)

M.q: Tess filed for presumptive death of her husband after asking only a few relatives about him. Which is TRUE?
o: Enough; the law requires only absence
Not enough; a well-founded belief requires diligent and reasonable search
Enough if she is in good faith
M.x: Republic v. Cantor.

M.q: Which can be corrected ADMINISTRATIVELY by the civil registrar?
o: Change of nationality in the birth certificate
Correction of the day and month of birth
Change of the year of birth
M.x: RA 9048 as amended by RA 10172: clerical errors, first name, day and month of birth, and sex if patently clerical. Substantial changes need Rule 108.

M.q: A person who underwent sex reassignment surgery asks the court to change the sex entry in the birth certificate. Which is TRUE?
o: Granted if the change is permanent
M.x: Silverio v. Republic; contrast Cagandahan (intersex).

M.q: Merla learns that records show her married to a foreigner she never met; her signature was forged. Her remedy is:
o: Petition to cancel the entries under Rule 108, in an adversarial proceeding
None; marriage records cannot be changed
M.x: Republic v. Olaybar.

P.title: Default regime and the marriage settlement
P.rule: Without a valid settlement executed before the marriage, ACP governs; a settlement binds third persons only if registered.

p.label: No settlement
p.facts: Lito and Mae married in 2022 without signing any marriage settlement. In 2025, Lito's creditor claims that Mae's salary cannot answer for family debts because their regime is conjugal partnership.
p.q: What is the property regime of Lito and Mae?
alac: Their regime is absolute community of property.
The law provides that in the absence of a marriage settlement, or when the regime agreed upon is void, the system of absolute community of property shall govern.
Here, Lito and Mae married in 2022 under the Family Code and signed no marriage settlement.
Therefore, their property relations are governed by absolute community of property, not conjugal partnership.
p.key: After August 3, 1988, the default is ACP. CPG is the default only for marriages before the Family Code without a settlement.

p.label: Settlement signed after the wedding
p.facts: Nico and Olga married on May 1. On May 5, they signed a notarized agreement adopting complete separation of property and registered it.
p.q: What regime governs their marriage?
p.hint: When must a settlement be executed?
alac: Absolute community of property governs.

The law provides that a marriage settlement must be in writing, signed by the parties, and executed before the celebration of the marriage; without a valid settlement, absolute community of property applies.
Here, Nico and Olga signed their agreement four days after the wedding. It was not executed before the marriage, so it is not a valid marriage settlement. Registration does not cure this.
Therefore, their regime is absolute community of property. They may only change it through judicial separation of property.
p.key: A post-wedding agreement cannot create a regime. Change during marriage needs a court (Arts. 76, 134–136).

p.label: Unregistered settlement and a creditor
p.facts: Before marrying, Paolo and Queenie signed a valid written settlement adopting complete separation of property, but never registered it. Paolo's creditor obtained a judgment and seeks to levy on a car registered in Queenie's name, bought during the marriage with her salary. Queenie invokes the settlement.
p.q: Can Queenie use the settlement against the creditor?
p.hint: Between whom does an unregistered settlement take effect?
alac: No. Queenie cannot use the settlement against the creditor.

The law provides that a marriage settlement shall not prejudice third persons unless it is registered in the local civil registry where the marriage contract is recorded and in the proper registries of property.

Here, the settlement is valid between Paolo and Queenie, but it was never registered. The creditor is a third person, so as to him the default regime, absolute community, applies, and the car bought during the marriage is community property.
Therefore, the creditor may levy on the car, subject to the rules on community liability for Paolo's debt.
p.key: TWIST: valid ≠ binding on third persons. Registration is what gives notice to creditors.

P.title: Revocation of donations propter nuptias
P.rule: A DPN in a settlement is void if the marriage does not take place; it is revocable on the Art. 86 grounds; and it is revoked by operation of law when the donee contracted a subsequent marriage in bad faith (or both acted in bad faith).

p.label: Wedding called off
p.facts: Two months before their wedding, Rick donated a condominium to his fiancée Sara in a separate notarized deed of donation, not in a marriage settlement. Sara accepted in the same deed. The wedding was called off.
p.q: What is the status of the donation?
p.hint: Was the donation in a marriage settlement?
alac: The donation is revocable.

The law provides that a donation by reason of marriage may be revoked by the donor if the marriage is not celebrated, except donations made in marriage settlements, which become void under the rule on settlements.
Here, Rick donated the condominium in consideration of the marriage, but in a separate deed, not in a marriage settlement. The marriage was not celebrated.
Therefore, the donation is revocable at Rick's instance. It is not automatically void.
p.key: In a SETTLEMENT + no marriage → VOID (Art. 81). In a separate deed + no marriage → REVOCABLE (Art. 86(1)).

p.label: Marriage without parental consent
p.facts: Tom and Uma, both 19, married without their parents' consent. Before the wedding, Tom's uncle donated a lot to Uma in consideration of the marriage.
p.q: May the uncle revoke the donation?
alac: Yes. The donation is revocable.
The law provides that a donation by reason of marriage may be revoked by the donor when the marriage takes place without the consent of the parents or guardians, as required by law.
Here, Tom and Uma were 19, so parental consent was required, and they married without it. The donation was made in consideration of that marriage.
Therefore, the uncle may revoke the donation.
p.key: Lack of parental consent (ages 18–21) is a ground to revoke, even though the marriage itself is only voidable.

p.label: Both parties in bad faith
p.facts: Vince's wife disappeared. Vince and Wena, knowing she was alive and living in Davao, conspired to obtain a declaration of presumptive death and married. Before the wedding, Vince donated a house to Wena by reason of the marriage.
p.q: What is the status of the donation?
p.hint: What happens when both parties to the subsequent marriage are in bad faith?
alac: The donation is revoked by operation of law.

The law provides that if both spouses of the subsequent marriage acted in bad faith, the marriage is void ab initio, and all donations by reason of marriage between them are revoked by operation of law.
Here, Vince and Wena both knew the first wife was alive and conspired to obtain the declaration. Both acted in bad faith.
Therefore, the donation to Wena is revoked by operation of law; no action to revoke is needed.
p.key: TWIST: “revocable” needs the donor to act; “revoked by operation of law” is automatic. Bad faith in the subsequent marriage → automatic.

P.title: Donations between spouses
P.rule: Donations between spouses during the marriage are void, except moderate gifts on occasions of family rejoicing; the rule also covers couples living together without a valid marriage.

p.label: Condominium as anniversary gift
p.facts: Yoyo and Zara, married under complete separation of property, celebrate their 10th anniversary. Yoyo transfers his P5 million condominium to Zara by deed of donation.
p.q: Is the donation valid?
alac: No. The donation is void.
The law provides that every donation or grant of gratuitous advantage between spouses during the marriage is void, except moderate gifts on the occasion of any family rejoicing.
Here, the donation was made during the marriage. A P5 million condominium is not a moderate gift. The fact that their regime is complete separation does not matter.
Therefore, the donation is void.
p.key: Art. 87 applies to ALL regimes. Past exam trap: “no limit under CPG or CSP” is FALSE.

p.label: Live-in partners
p.facts: Al and Bea live together without marriage. Al donates his car to Bea on her birthday.
p.q: Is the donation valid?
alac: No. The donation is void.

The law provides that the prohibition on donations between spouses also applies to persons living together as husband and wife without a valid marriage, except moderate gifts on occasions of family rejoicing.
Here, Al and Bea live together as husband and wife without marriage. A car is not a moderate gift.
Therefore, the donation is void.
p.key: The prohibition extends to cohabiting couples, to prevent them from getting a better position than married spouses.

p.label: Moderate birthday gift
p.facts: On his wife's birthday, Carl gives her a P15,000 necklace. The couple's monthly income is P250,000.
p.q: Is the gift valid?
alac: Yes. The gift is valid.
The law provides that donations between spouses during the marriage are void, except moderate gifts which the spouses may give each other on the occasion of any family rejoicing.
Here, the gift was given on the wife's birthday, an occasion of family rejoicing. A P15,000 necklace is moderate considering their income.
Therefore, the gift is valid.
p.key: TWIST: two requisites for the exception: (1) moderate, judged by the family's means; (2) on family rejoicing.

P.title: Classifying property under ACP
P.rule: All property owned at the time of the marriage or acquired after is community property, except gratuitous acquisitions (and their fruits), property for personal use (except jewelry), and pre-marriage property of a spouse with legitimate descendants by a former marriage.

p.label: Pre-marriage lot
p.facts: Dina owned a lot before marrying Eli in 2019. They have no marriage settlement. Dina has no children from any previous relationship. In 2026, Dina claims the lot is hers alone.
p.q: Is the lot Dina's exclusive property?
p.hint: Under ACP, does pre-marriage property stay exclusive?
alac: No. The lot is community property.

The law provides that the community property consists of all the property owned by the spouses at the time of the celebration of the marriage or acquired thereafter, except the property excluded by law.

Here, their regime is ACP because they have no settlement. Dina owned the lot at the time of the marriage. She has no legitimate descendants by a former marriage, and the lot is not a gratuitous acquisition during the marriage.
Therefore, the lot became community property.
p.key: Under ACP, “mine before the wedding” is not a defense, unless the spouse has LEGITIMATE descendants by a former marriage.

p.label: Inheritance and its rent
p.facts: During the marriage, under ACP, Fe inherited an apartment from her mother. Her mother's will is silent on whether it goes to the community. The apartment earns P30,000 a month in rent.
p.q: Who owns the apartment and the rent?
alac: Both the apartment and the rent are Fe's exclusive property.

The law provides that property acquired during the marriage by gratuitous title, as well as its fruits and income, is excluded from the community, unless the donor or testator expressly provides otherwise.
Here, Fe acquired the apartment by inheritance, a gratuitous title, during the marriage. The will does not say it forms part of the community.
Therefore, the apartment and its rent are Fe's exclusive property.
p.key: Under ACP, fruits of gratuitously acquired property are excluded too. Under CPG, they would be conjugal.

p.label: Jewelry for personal use
p.facts: Using community funds, Gelo buys a P400,000 diamond ring for himself, which only he wears. Upon dissolution, he claims it as exclusive property for his personal use.
p.q: Is the ring Gelo's exclusive property?
p.hint: Is there an exception to the personal-use exclusion?
alac: No. The ring is community property.
The law provides that property for the personal and exclusive use of either spouse is excluded from the community, but jewelry shall form part of the community property.
Here, the ring is for Gelo's personal and exclusive use, but it is jewelry.
Therefore, the ring is community property, even though only Gelo uses it.
p.key: TWIST: personal use excludes clothes, a car, and the like, but NEVER jewelry.

P.title: Charges on the community
P.rule: The ACP answers for support, family-benefit debts, repairs, self-improvement courses, donations by both spouses to common children, and other listed charges; debts without consent bind it only to the extent the family benefited.

p.label: Loan for the family business
p.facts: Under ACP, Hilda alone borrows P500,000 from a bank to expand the family's sari-sari store. Her husband did not sign. The loan is unpaid.
p.q: Is the community liable for the loan?
p.hint: Debts without consent: when do they bind the community?
alac: Yes. The community is liable.

The law provides that the absolute community is liable for debts contracted by either spouse without the consent of the other to the extent that the family may have been benefited. Jurisprudence provides that a loan for the spouse's own business is presumed to benefit the family.
Here, Hilda borrowed the money for the family's store, which supports the family. The benefit to the family is presumed.
Therefore, the community is liable for the loan.
p.key: Own business → benefit presumed. Surety for another's business → must be proved.

p.label: Husband's law school
p.facts: During the marriage, Ivan enrolls in law school. His tuition is paid from community funds. His wife objects that it benefits only him.
p.q: Is the tuition chargeable to the community?
alac: Yes. The tuition is chargeable to the community.
The law provides that the absolute community is liable for expenses to enable either spouse to commence or complete a professional or vocational course, or other activity for self-improvement.
Here, Ivan's law school tuition is an expense to complete a professional course.
Therefore, it is chargeable to the community.
p.key: Self-improvement of EITHER spouse is a community charge.

p.label: One spouse's gift to a child
p.facts: Under ACP, Joy alone, without her husband's knowledge, gives P50,000 from community funds to their legitimate son for a coding bootcamp. The husband says the community should not bear it.
p.q: Is the donation chargeable to the community?
alac: No. It is not chargeable to the community as such.

The law provides that the community is liable for the value of what is donated or promised by both spouses in favor of their common legitimate children for the exclusive purpose of a professional or vocational course or other activity for self-improvement.
Here, the course is for self-improvement, but only Joy made the donation. The requirement that both spouses donate is not met.
Therefore, the donation is not a charge on the community; it is chargeable to Joy.
p.key: TWIST: the word is BOTH spouses. Past exam asked exactly this.

P.title: Disposition without the other spouse's consent
P.rule: Disposition or encumbrance of community or conjugal property without the other spouse's written consent or court authority is void, but it is a continuing offer that becomes binding upon acceptance before withdrawal.

p.label: Mortgage behind the wife's back
p.facts: Under CPG, Kiko mortgaged their conjugal house to a bank without his wife's knowledge or consent. The loan was unpaid and the bank foreclosed. The bank argues the mortgage is valid at least as to Kiko's half.
p.q: Is the mortgage valid as to Kiko's half?
p.hint: Does a spouse have a definite share before liquidation?
alac: No. The mortgage is void in its entirety.

The law provides that a disposition or encumbrance of conjugal property without the written consent of the other spouse or authority of the court is void. Jurisprudence provides that a spouse has no definite share in conjugal property until liquidation, so the encumbrance is void as a whole.
Here, Kiko mortgaged the conjugal house without his wife's consent or court authority. He has no specific half to mortgage before liquidation.
Therefore, the mortgage is void in its entirety.
p.key: Void as a WHOLE, not just as to the other spouse's half (Dailo).

p.label: Later acceptance
p.facts: Under ACP, Lando sold a community lot to Mon without his wife's consent. Before Mon withdrew, the wife signed a written acceptance of the sale.
p.q: Is the sale binding?
alac: Yes. The sale is binding.

The law provides that a disposition without the other spouse's consent is void, but the transaction shall be construed as a continuing offer that may be perfected as a binding contract upon the acceptance by the other spouse before the offer is withdrawn.
Here, the wife accepted the sale in writing before Mon withdrew.
Therefore, a binding contract was perfected.
p.key: Void + continuing offer → binding upon acceptance BEFORE withdrawal.

p.label: Sale of exclusive property under CPG
p.facts: Under CPG, Nina sells a lot she inherited from her father, without her husband's consent.
p.q: Is the sale void for lack of the husband's consent?
p.hint: What kind of property is it under CPG?
alac: No. The sale is valid.

The law provides that under the conjugal partnership, property acquired by gratuitous title during the marriage is the exclusive property of the spouse, and a spouse may alienate his or her exclusive property without the consent of the other.
Here, the lot was inherited, so it is Nina's exclusive property under CPG. The consent requirement applies only to conjugal property.
Therefore, the sale is valid.
p.key: TWIST: consent is needed for COMMUNITY or CONJUGAL property only.

P.title: Failure to liquidate after death
P.rule: After a spouse's death, the community must be liquidated within one year if there is no judicial settlement; otherwise dispositions of community property are void and a subsequent marriage is governed by mandatory complete separation.

p.label: Widow remarries
p.facts: Olive's husband died in March 2023. There was no judicial settlement, and she never liquidated their community. She married Pete in 2025 without a settlement.
p.q: What is the regime of Olive and Pete?
p.hint: What happens if the survivor remarries without liquidating?
alac: Their regime is complete separation of property.

The law provides that if the surviving spouse contracts a subsequent marriage without liquidating the community within one year from the death of the deceased spouse, the subsequent marriage shall be governed by a regime of complete separation of property.
Here, Olive did not liquidate within one year after her husband's death in 2023 and remarried in 2025.
Therefore, her marriage to Pete is mandatorily governed by complete separation of property.
p.key: Mandatory CSP overrides the default ACP.

p.label: Sale before liquidation
p.facts: Quino's wife died in 2022. In 2024, without any liquidation, he sold a community lot.
p.q: Is the sale valid?
alac: No. The sale is void.
The law provides that if no liquidation is made within one year from the death, any disposition or encumbrance involving the community property of the terminated marriage shall be void.
Here, Quino sold the community lot in 2024, more than one year after his wife's death, without liquidation.
Therefore, the sale is void.
p.key: After one year without liquidation, dispositions are void.

p.label: Liquidated on time
p.facts: Rosa's husband died in January 2024. In October 2024, she executed an extrajudicial liquidation of their community and registered it. In 2025, she married Sid without a settlement.
p.q: What is the regime of Rosa and Sid?
p.hint: Was the liquidation done within the period?
alac: Their regime is absolute community of property.

The law provides that mandatory separation of property applies only if the survivor remarries without liquidating within one year; otherwise, in the absence of a settlement, absolute community applies.
Here, Rosa liquidated the community within one year from her husband's death, before remarrying. She and Sid had no settlement.
Therefore, the default absolute community of property governs.
p.key: TWIST: timely liquidation removes the penalty.

P.title: Classifying property under CPG
P.rule: Under CPG, property brought into the marriage, gratuitous acquisitions, and property bought with exclusive money stay exclusive; earnings, fruits, and onerous acquisitions with common funds are conjugal; improvements follow Art. 120.

p.label: Car bought with exclusive money
p.facts: Tess and Ulan married in 1985 without a settlement, so CPG applies. In 2024, Tess sold a lot she inherited and used the entire proceeds to buy a car in her name.
p.q: Is the car conjugal property?
alac: No. The car is Tess's exclusive property.
The law provides that property purchased with the exclusive money of the wife or of the husband is exclusive property under the conjugal partnership.
Here, Tess bought the car entirely with the proceeds of her inherited lot, which was her exclusive property.
Therefore, the car is her exclusive property.
p.key: Pre-1988 marriages without a settlement are CPG. Under CPG, exclusive money buys exclusive property.

p.label: Salary and rent
p.facts: Under CPG, Vic earns a salary and also collects rent from a building he owned before the marriage.
p.q: Are the salary and the rent conjugal property?
alac: Yes. Both the salary and the net rent are conjugal property.

The law provides that conjugal property includes property obtained from the labor, industry, work, or profession of either spouse, and the net fruits from the exclusive property of each spouse received during the marriage.
Here, Vic's salary comes from his work, and the rent is a fruit of his exclusive building received during the marriage.
Therefore, the salary and the net rent are conjugal, while the building stays his exclusive property.
p.key: Under CPG the building stays exclusive, but its NET fruits are conjugal.

p.label: Big improvement on a small lot
